items.goal: Explain what an LLM is, what it learns from, and what it can do.

points.title: Full Meaning
points.explanation: LLM stands for Large Language Model.
points.sentence: LLM stands for Large Language Model, which is a type of artificial intelligence.

points.title: Training
points.explanation: LLMs are trained on large amounts of text and sometimes other types of data.
points.sentence: These models learn patterns from large collections of text and, in some cases, other data.

points.title: Language Tasks
points.explanation: An LLM can process questions, generate text, and help explain information.
points.sentence: An LLM can help us understand questions, create written responses, and explain different topics.

points.title: Important Limitation
points.explanation: An LLM can produce incorrect information, so important answers should be checked.
points.sentence: However, its answers are not always correct, so important information should be verified.

items.professionalResponse:
LLM stands for Large Language Model, a type of AI trained on large amounts of text and sometimes other data.
It can understand language patterns, answer questions, and generate useful written content.
However, important information should still be checked for accuracy.

items.goal: Explain the basic working process of a language model in simple English.

points.title: Input Processing
points.explanation: The model receives and processes the user's input.
points.sentence: First, the model processes the information or question provided by the user.

points.title: Tokens
points.explanation: Text is represented using smaller units called tokens.
points.sentence: The model works with tokens, which are smaller units of text.

points.title: Predicting the Next Token
points.explanation: The model uses learned patterns and available context to select tokens that form a response.
points.sentence: It uses learned patterns and the available context to predict the next token, building the response step by step.

points.title: Accuracy
points.explanation: Generating a fluent answer does not automatically mean the information has been verified.
points.sentence: Although the response may sound natural, the model does not automatically verify every statement.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM processes your input and works with smaller units of text called tokens.
It uses learned patterns and available context to generate a response step by step.
The response may be useful and natural, but its factual accuracy is not automatically guaranteed.

items.goal: Describe practical uses of an LLM without exaggerating its capabilities.

points.title: Writing
points.explanation: An LLM can assist with emails, messages, reports, and other written material.
points.sentence: One useful application is writing support, such as preparing emails, messages, and reports.

points.title: Summarization
points.explanation: An LLM can summarize documents and simplify complicated information.
points.sentence: It can also summarize long documents and explain difficult information in simpler language.

points.title: Translation and Learning
points.explanation: An LLM can help translate text and explain new concepts.
points.sentence: Another useful application is language translation and learning support.

points.title: Technical Assistance
points.explanation: Some models can assist with coding, analysis, and complex tasks, but their output should be reviewed.
points.sentence: Some models can also support coding and analysis, although the results should be checked.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM can help with writing, summarizing documents, explaining concepts, and translating text.
Some models can also assist with coding, analysis, and other technical tasks.
It is a useful support tool, but important results should always be reviewed.

items.goal: Explain the difference between generated responses and retrieved information.

points.title: Search Engines
points.explanation: Search engines help users find information from indexed sources.
points.sentence: A search engine helps us find information from websites and other indexed sources.

points.title: Language Models
points.explanation: An LLM generates responses using learned patterns and available context.
points.sentence: An LLM works differently because it generates a response using learned patterns and the information available to it.

points.title: Connected Search
points.explanation: Some AI applications connect language models to external search tools.
points.sentence: Some AI applications can also use search tools to access additional information.

points.title: Verification
points.explanation: Generated answers and retrieved sources should be evaluated appropriately.
points.sentence: For factual questions, it is useful to check whether reliable sources support the answer.

items.professionalResponse:
No, an LLM and a search engine work differently.
A search engine finds information from indexed sources, while an LLM generates responses using learned patterns and context.
Some AI applications combine both capabilities, depending on their available tools.

items.goal: Explain the knowledge limitations of language models.

points.title: Limited Knowledge
points.explanation: An LLM does not have complete knowledge of every topic.
points.sentence: An LLM can provide information on many subjects, but it does not know everything.

points.title: Recent Events
points.explanation: A model may not have access to the latest events or developments.
points.sentence: It may not know about recent events unless the application provides access to current information.

points.title: Specialized Information
points.explanation: Some specialized or private information may not be available to the model.
points.sentence: It may also lack specialized information or private documents that have not been provided to it.

points.title: Accuracy
points.explanation: Even familiar information may occasionally be incorrect.
points.sentence: Even when the model is familiar with a topic, its answer is not guaranteed to be accurate.

items.professionalResponse:
No, an LLM does not know everything about the world.
Its knowledge may be limited, especially for recent events, specialized subjects, or private information.
Important answers should be checked against reliable sources.

items.goal: Explain why confidence and accuracy are different.

points.title: Confident Language
points.explanation: An LLM may sound certain even when some information is wrong.
points.sentence: First, a confident tone does not always mean the information is correct.

points.title: Missing Verification
points.explanation: The model does not automatically verify every statement against reliable evidence.
points.sentence: Another important point is that the answer may not have been independently verified.

points.title: Incomplete Context
points.explanation: The model may be missing information that could affect its answer.
points.sentence: It is also possible that the model does not have all the relevant information.

points.title: Check Important Facts
points.explanation: Important claims should be checked using appropriate sources.
points.sentence: For important decisions, I recommend checking the information against reliable sources.

items.professionalResponse:
Not necessarily. An LLM can sound confident even when its answer contains incorrect information.
The response may not have been independently verified, and important context could be missing.
For important decisions, we recommend checking the answer against reliable sources.

items.goal: Explain the difference between language-model processing and human experience.

points.title: Learned Language Patterns
points.explanation: An LLM learns complex relationships and patterns from training data.
points.sentence: An LLM learns complex language patterns from the data used during training.

points.title: Language Processing
points.explanation: It can process questions and produce meaningful responses.
points.sentence: This allows it to answer questions and generate responses that often sound natural.

points.title: Human Experience
points.explanation: Human understanding involves lived experience and interaction with the world.
points.sentence: Human understanding also involves personal experiences and interaction with the real world.

points.title: Important Difference
points.explanation: Human-like language does not establish that the model understands things exactly as humans do.
points.sentence: Therefore, natural-sounding language does not mean an LLM understands the world in the same way people do.

items.professionalResponse:
Not exactly. An LLM learns complex patterns and relationships in language.
This helps it produce meaningful responses and perform many useful language tasks.
However, that does not mean it has human experiences or understands the world in the same way people do.

items.goal: Explain model reasoning capabilities and their limitations.

points.title: Complex Tasks
points.explanation: Some LLMs can solve challenging problems.
points.sentence: Some language models can work through complex questions and solve difficult tasks.

points.title: Step-by-Step Analysis
points.explanation: Models can provide explanations and structured approaches to problems.
points.sentence: They can also provide structured explanations and help organize problem-solving steps.

points.title: Reasoning Mistakes
points.explanation: A model may make logical mistakes even when its explanation sounds convincing.
points.sentence: However, a model can make reasoning mistakes, even when the explanation sounds convincing.

points.title: Independent Checking
points.explanation: Important reasoning and conclusions should be reviewed.
points.sentence: For important problems, I recommend checking the reasoning and final conclusion.

items.professionalResponse:
Yes, some LLMs can solve complex problems and perform useful reasoning tasks.
They can help organize information and provide structured explanations.
However, they may make logical mistakes, so important conclusions should be verified.

items.goal: Explain training knowledge, conversation context, and connected information sources.

points.title: Training Data
points.explanation: An LLM uses patterns learned during training.
points.sentence: One source is the information patterns the model learned during its training.

points.title: Current Conversation
points.explanation: The user's current input and available conversation context influence the response.
points.sentence: The model also uses the information provided in the current conversation.

points.title: Connected Documents
points.explanation: Some applications can provide access to approved documents or knowledge sources.
points.sentence: Depending on the application, the model may also receive information from connected documents.

points.title: External Tools
points.explanation: Some AI applications can use external tools, subject to their permissions.
points.sentence: Certain applications can also use external tools to retrieve additional information when access is available.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM uses patterns learned during training and information provided in the current conversation.
Depending on the application, it may also access connected documents or external tools.
The information available to the model depends on the system and its permissions.

items.goal: Explain why repeated answers are not independent evidence.

points.title: Repeated Output
points.explanation: An AI system may generate the same answer more than once.
points.sentence: An AI system may provide the same answer when a question is repeated.

points.title: Repetition Is Not Proof
points.explanation: Repeating a claim does not establish factual accuracy.
points.sentence: However, getting the same answer twice does not prove that the information is correct.

points.title: Independent Evidence
points.explanation: Reliable verification requires evidence separate from the model's repeated claim.
points.sentence: To verify the answer, we need evidence from an appropriate independent source.

points.title: Source Relevance
points.explanation: The source must actually support the specific statement.
points.sentence: It is also important to confirm that the source directly supports the information being checked.

items.professionalResponse:
No, receiving the same AI answer twice does not mean it has been verified.
Repeated responses are not independent evidence of factual accuracy.
To verify the information, please check it against a reliable source that directly supports the claim.

items.goal: Explain when current information may be available.

points.title: Knowledge Limitations
points.explanation: An LLM may not have information about very recent events.
points.sentence: An LLM may not automatically know about events that happened today.

points.title: Connected Search Tools
points.explanation: Some AI applications can retrieve current information.
points.sentence: Some AI applications have search tools that can access more recent information.

points.title: Application Capabilities
points.explanation: Availability of current information depends on the specific application.
points.sentence: Whether current information is available depends on the tools connected to the application.

points.title: Reliable Sources
points.explanation: Recent claims should be checked for dates, accuracy, and source quality.
points.sentence: For recent events, I recommend checking the publication date and a reliable supporting source.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM may not automatically know about events that happened today.
Some AI applications can access current information through connected search tools or other sources.
For recent events, please check whether the application has up-to-date access and verify the information.

items.goal: Explain hallucinations without unnecessary technical complexity.

points.title: Hallucination
points.explanation: An LLM may generate incorrect or unsupported information.
points.sentence: This type of incorrect or unsupported AI-generated information is often called a hallucination.

points.title: Fluent Language
points.explanation: A response can sound natural even when some facts are wrong.
points.sentence: The model may produce fluent language even when the information is inaccurate.

points.title: Generation Versus Verification
points.explanation: Producing a response is not the same as checking its factual accuracy.
points.sentence: Generating a response and verifying that response are two different processes.

points.title: Better Checking
points.explanation: Reliable sources can help identify unsupported claims.
points.sentence: For important information, we should compare the answer with reliable supporting evidence.

items.professionalResponse:
This can happen when an LLM generates incorrect or unsupported information, often called a hallucination.
A fluent and convincing response does not necessarily mean the facts have been verified.
For important information, we recommend checking the answer against reliable sources.

items.goal: Explain how to use AI assistance responsibly for calculations.

points.title: Mathematical Assistance
points.explanation: An LLM can help explain formulas and mathematical problems.
points.sentence: An LLM can help explain calculations, formulas, and mathematical steps.

points.title: Possible Errors
points.explanation: The model may make arithmetic or reasoning mistakes.
points.sentence: However, it can sometimes make errors in calculations or mathematical reasoning.

points.title: Calculation Tools
points.explanation: Calculators and spreadsheets can verify numerical results.
points.sentence: For numerical accuracy, I recommend checking the result with a calculator or spreadsheet.

points.title: Financial Decisions
points.explanation: Important financial decisions need reliable figures and appropriate review.
points.sentence: When financial decisions are involved, the figures should be verified before they are used.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM can help explain calculations and work through mathematical problems.
However, it may make numerical or reasoning mistakes.
For important financial figures, please verify the results using a reliable calculation tool.

items.goal: Explain the benefits and limitations of AI-assisted document understanding.

points.title: Simple Explanations
points.explanation: An LLM can help explain complicated terminology.
points.sentence: An LLM can help explain difficult legal or medical terms in simpler language.

points.title: Document Summaries
points.explanation: It can help summarize long documents.
points.sentence: It can also summarize long documents to make them easier to review.

points.title: Interpretation Risks
points.explanation: The model may misunderstand important details.
points.sentence: However, the model may misunderstand or overlook important information.

points.title: Professional Judgment
points.explanation: Qualified professionals should review matters requiring expert judgment.
points.sentence: For important legal or medical decisions, a qualified professional should review the relevant information.

items.professionalResponse:
Yes, an LLM can help explain difficult terms and summarize legal or medical documents.
However, it may misunderstand important details or provide incomplete explanations.
For decisions requiring expert judgment, please consult a qualified professional.

items.goal: Explain when external evidence is necessary and when it may not be.

points.title: Creative Tasks
points.explanation: Fictional writing and creative text may not need internet research.
points.sentence: Creative tasks, such as writing a fictional greeting, do not necessarily require an internet search.

points.title: Rewriting Tasks
points.explanation: Rewriting supplied text can often be completed using the provided information.
points.sentence: If we are rewriting text already provided by the user, an external search may not be necessary.

points.title: Real-World Claims
points.explanation: Statements about payments, dates, orders, and policies may need evidence.
points.sentence: However, claims about real transactions, dates, or policies should be checked against appropriate records.

points.title: Appropriate Verification
points.explanation: The correct verification method depends on the task.
points.sentence: The most suitable verification method depends on what the user wants to confirm.

items.professionalResponse:
No, not every AI-generated response requires an internet search.
Creative writing or rewriting supplied text may only need a review of the content.
However, claims about real-world facts, payments, dates, or policies should be checked against appropriate evidence.

items.goal: Teach learners how to explain effective prompting in simple English.

points.title: Clear Request
points.explanation: Explain exactly what help is needed.
points.sentence: First, try to explain clearly what you want the AI to help you with.

points.title: Relevant Context
points.explanation: Provide background information that helps the model understand the task.
points.sentence: It also helps to provide relevant context so the model can better understand your situation.

points.title: Desired Format
points.explanation: Tell the model how the answer should be organized.
points.sentence: You can also specify whether you want a short explanation, a table, or step-by-step instructions.

points.title: Specific Example
points.explanation: A focused request is often more useful than a very broad question.
points.sentence: For example, instead of saying 'Explain AI,' you could ask 'Explain AI to a beginner using three simple examples.'

items.professionalResponse:
To get a more useful answer, explain your request clearly and include relevant context.
You can also describe the format, level of detail, or audience you prefer.
For example, ask the AI to explain a topic to a beginner using three simple examples.

items.goal: Teach safe, accurate, and professional AI-assisted customer support.

points.title: Incorrect Information
points.explanation: AI-generated responses may contain mistakes.
points.sentence: The first thing to consider is that an AI-generated response may contain incorrect information.

points.title: Customer Context
points.explanation: The model may misunderstand the customer's actual situation.
points.sentence: Another important point is that the model may misunderstand the customer's specific issue.

points.title: Data Protection
points.explanation: Sensitive customer information should only be handled through authorized systems.
points.sentence: We should also protect customer information and follow the organization's data-handling policies.

points.title: Reliable Verification
points.explanation: Important responses should be checked before being shared.
points.sentence: Before sending an important response, we should verify it using reliable reference material.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM can help draft customer replies, but its responses may contain errors or misunderstand the customer's situation.
Customer information must be handled according to the organization's privacy and access rules.
Important answers should be verified against reliable reference material before being shared.

items.goal: Summarize responsible and practical AI usage.

points.title: Powerful Tool
points.explanation: An LLM can support many useful tasks.
points.sentence: The most important thing to remember is that an LLM is a powerful tool that can support different types of work.

points.title: Accuracy Is Not Guaranteed
points.explanation: A convincing answer may still be inaccurate.
points.sentence: However, a convincing AI-generated response is not always a verified fact.

points.title: Human Judgment
points.explanation: People should evaluate AI-generated information before relying on it.
points.sentence: Human judgment remains important when reviewing AI-generated information.

points.title: Responsible Use
points.explanation: Important information and decisions should be supported by appropriate evidence.
points.sentence: For responsible use, we should check important information before making decisions.

items.professionalResponse:
An LLM is a powerful language tool that can support learning, communication, and many practical tasks.
However, a convincing AI-generated answer is not necessarily a verified fact.
Use AI to support your work, check important information, and apply human judgment when making decisions.
